stem.text: The amount of water in a storage tank is modeled by \( W(t) = 10 + 20 e^{- \frac{t}{12}} \) hundreds of gallons, for \( 0 \le t \le 36 \), where t is measured in hours. Using a calculator, find \( W'(9) \), showing the setup, and interpret the value in the context of the problem with correct units. Give the value correct to three decimal places.

answer_key.label: \( W'(9) = -0.787 \), so at time t = 9 hours the amount of water in the tank is decreasing at a rate of 0.787 hundreds of gallons per hour.

worked_solution.text: Differentiate the model to get the rate, \( W'(t) = - \frac{5 e^{- \frac{t}{12}}}{3} \).
With a calculator, \( W'(9) = -0.787 \) to three decimal places.
worked_solution.rule_named: evaluate the derivative at the instant

worked_solution.text: The value is negative, so at time t = 9 hours the amount of water in the tank is decreasing at a rate of 0.787 hundreds of gallons per hour.
worked_solution.rule_named: sign of the rate gives the direction of change
